tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local continuation fixture derived from the prior multi_agent checkpoint. Worker W1 has a stable effect_identity=E and intended payload H1 after acknowledgement_lost_after_possible_commit. The checkpoint also preserves the last authoritative claim observation for E as generation 12, payload H1, owner W1. A later authoritative lookup returns E at monotonic generation 13 with payload H2 and owner W2. The fixture verifies only whether W1 may attribute its lost-ack operation as success, retry create, retry overwrite, or otherwise mutate E after observing the newer canonical generation. No public-source probe, O/downstream or other-worker semantics, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, real simultaneous repository write, richer-mode arbitration, external coordinator, or optional second semantic leaf was used.

reconciliation_result.required_action: preserve generation 13 state, classify W1 outcome as unresolved/non-attributable, and require any future W1 action to re-enter through a fresh atomic claim against the current generation rather than replaying the lost-ack mutation

observations: A monotonic generation increase from 12 to 13 proves that the canonical claim state advanced after W1's checkpoint and that the later H2/W2 record is newer than the checkpointed H1/W1 record.
Because the current canonical owner is W2 and payload H2 differs from W1's intended H1, W1 cannot safely infer that its acknowledgement-lost operation is the currently canonical success.
The safe replay rule suppresses both create and overwrite retries by W1; stable effect identity does not grant ownership once a newer canonical generation is observed.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, an authoritative monotonic generation fence plus current-owner identity is sufficient to reject a stale worker's replay after acknowledgement loss when a newer conflicting canonical state is observed. It prevents duplicate/conflicting mutation without external hosted coordination or richer-mode arbitration. This fixture does not prove that any concrete allowed repository/API transport exposes the required atomic claim, monotonic generation, or owner semantics, and it does not prove liveness if fresh claim acquisition remains unavailable.
unresolved_children: Availability of an atomic single-winner claim primitive keyed by stable effect identity on an allowed zero-cost quota-independent transport remains unproven.
A real allowed transport exposing authoritative monotonic generation plus current-owner identity remains unproven.
The same-payload ABA branch remains untested: a later record may carry payload H1 again under a newer generation/owner, so payload equality alone may still be unsafe for success attribution.
No liveness claim is made when fresh atomic claim acquisition remains unavailable or indefinitely contended.
